conventions.convention: The scaled Chebyshev filter assumes a>b>c and integer k≥0; T₀=1, and its positive exterior normalization gives a polynomial of degree exactly k.
Finite-precision statements concern successful real operationwise arithmetic: exact-zero operations are permitted, nonzero exact intermediates must be normal-range, and γk=ku/(1−ku) requires ku<1.

Two-pass MGS uses two complete sequential passes; vector updates use a rounded product followed by a rounded subtraction. Positive normalization and successful operations are hypotheses, and the orthogonality conclusion is an explicit a posteriori recurrence rather than an unconditional small-error guarantee.
The CG gap is stored recursive residual minus exact true residual, gⱼ=r̂ⱼ−(b−Ax̂ⱼ); its bounds use actual stored αk and include the initial gap.

Lanczos eigenvalues are ordered decreasingly; r is the full top-eigenvalue multiplicity, P projects onto that eigenspace, and θm is defined variationally for every m≥1, including after exact breakdown. All convergence and breakdown conclusions are exact-arithmetic statements.

The GMRES coordinate residual g is evaluated from stored coefficients; no least-squares accuracy is assumed. The true-residual bound includes initial-vector, Arnoldi-relation, and final-update errors.
The GMRES cost bound assumes canonical square CSR with every row nonempty, s=nnz(A), exact arithmetic and 1≤m≤n; it excludes input-matrix storage and an earlier-breakdown fallback solve.

load_bearing.statement: For real symmetric A, unit b, top-eigenspace projection P and largest Rayleigh–Ritz value θm: if Pb=0, θm≤λr+1; if Pb≠0 and λr+1>λn, 0≤λ1−θm≤(λ1−λn)τ²/Tm−1(1+2(λ1−λr+1)/(λr+1−λn))², where τ=‖(I−P)b‖₂/‖Pb‖₂. Separate clauses handle scalar matrices, a collapsed unwanted interval, and exact invariant-subspace breakdown.

Under the specified successful real two-pass MGS operations, nu<1, γn<1, 2u<1 and tⱼ>0, Aqⱼ=Σi≤j hᵢⱼqᵢ+βⱼ₊₁qⱼ₊₁+eⱼ, with explicit operation-error bounds. For full-column-rank generated vectors, the displayed recurrence bounds their off-diagonal inner products and Frobenius Gram defect.
For a>b>c and integer k≥0, pₖ(x)=Tₖ((2x−b−c)/(b−c))/Tₖ((2a−b−c)/(b−c)) has degree exactly k, pₖ(a)=1, and maxx∈[c,b]|pₖ(x)|=1/Tₖ((2a−b−c)/(b−c)).

For the stated successful computed CG steps on a real SPD system, ‖gⱼ‖₂≤Γⱼ and ‖b−Ax̂ⱼ‖₂≤‖r̂ⱼ‖₂+Γⱼ; consequently ‖x*−x̂ⱼ‖A≤(‖r̂ⱼ‖₂+Γⱼ)/√λmin. The statement supplies explicit matvec and update error bounds and asserts neither exact-grade termination nor true-residual monotonicity.

concerns.concern: The title says “Unrestarted GMRES solves a two-dimensional diagonal system before GMRES(1) restarts”. The verification instead shows that the first GMRES step has nonzero residual, GMRES(1) then restarts, and unrestarted GMRES solves at step 2. The phrase “before GMRES(1) restarts” misstates that timing; the Example and calculations themselves are correct.

alerts.finding: In ex-trace-eigenspace-optimization-with-lanczos-start-angle, the Example says: “The Chebyshev start-angle bound gives an upper bound $5/8$ for the same Rayleigh quotient gap, so this explicit candidate satisfies it.” The cited thm-lanczos-largest-ritz-value-chebyshev-bound-with-degenerate-cases bounds λ1−θ2, where θ2 is the maximum quotient on K2, rather than the gap of an arbitrary candidate in K2. Proof 3.1 correctly applies the theorem to θ2. The candidate inequality is independently true because Proof 2.1 computes its gap as 4/9≤5/8, but the Example's attribution conflates these two gaps.
